$comment: The two product repositories this one orchestrates, and the exact commit of each.
This file is the single source of truth for that. `./deps.sh` reads it to place
the checkouts locally; every workflow under .github/workflows reads it in its
`resolve` job and feeds the refs to actions/checkout. Change a ref here and both
move together — there is nowhere else to update.
`ref` is what is actually checked out and should stay a full commit SHA: that is
what makes a build reproducible, and what lets a red run be traced to a specific
commit of a specific dependency rather than to whatever `main` was that hour.
`branch` is only what `./deps.sh --update` reads when asked to move a pin forward;
nothing checks it out on its own.
Moving a pin is a deliberate step, taken by running the checks:
./deps.sh --update            resolve each branch to its head and rewrite `ref`
cd common && bun run check    prove the new pins pass before committing them

dependencies.name: app-with-ai-tanstack
needed_for: language/cli/src/generate/jdm.ts imports packages/web/src/lib/jdm-converter.ts and mermaid-flowchart-parser.ts across the repository boundary, on every generation path — so every --stack target needs this checkout, not just the heavy one
language/cli/src/generate/tanstack.ts resolves packages/generator/src/pipeline/generate-application.ts at runtime, which is what --stack tanstack-nestjs drives

build/reporting-pack.ts imports packages/generator/src/reporting/pack.ts — the pack derivation lives there now, because the generated application's browser build and its deployable archive read the same one
that pipeline needs this repository's own dependencies installed, so the checkout is followed by `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in it
docker-compose.yml builds app-backend and app-frontend from the application generated by it

dependencies.name: enterprise_reporting_tanstack
dependencies.install_note: Nothing local reads this checkout's node_modules — it is a Docker build context, and the image build runs its own install inside the image, so `./deps.sh --install` skips it.
needed_for: docker-compose.yml builds the `report` and `seeder` services from this checkout as their build context, with common/ passed as an additional context

scripts/seed-reporting-pack.ts in that repository is the seeder both this orchestrator and a generated application's own compose file run — it uses that project's real getDb, encrypt and introspectAndCacheSchema rather than a second implementation of any of them
